what_its_for: Alemtuzumab is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults, including relapsing-remitting MS. It works by targeting and reducing certain white blood cells (called lymphocytes) that are attacking your nervous system. It is usually only used when at least two other MS medicines have not worked well enough. Campath is also used to treat a certain type of blood cancer called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).
how_to_take: Alemtuzumab is NOT a pill you take at home. It is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion — meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle — by a healthcare provider in a certified medical facility. Each infusion session takes about 4 hours. You will be watched closely by medical staff during and after each infusion for any reactions. You will also be given other medicines (such as steroids and antihistamines) before each infusion to help reduce side effects.
dosing: For MS (Lemtrada): The treatment is given in two separate courses. Course 1 is 5 days in a row (once daily for 5 consecutive days). Course 2 happens about 12 months later and is 3 days in a row (once daily for 3 consecutive days). Some patients may need a third or fourth course, each separated by 12 months if needed. For CLL (Campath): Dosing is different and will be determined by your cancer doctor (oncologist) based on your individual situation. Always follow the schedule your doctor sets for you.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a medical facility, missing an appointment is very different from missing a pill at home. If you need to reschedule or miss an infusion appointment, call your doctor or treatment center as soon as possible. Do NOT try to catch up on your own. Your doctor will reschedule your infusion and make sure your treatment stays on track safely.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home — it is prepared and stored by the medical facility. If for any reason you are given information about storage, know that unopened vials should be kept refrigerated at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C), protected from light, and should NOT be frozen. Diluted solutions for infusion should be used within 8 hours of preparation.
what_to_avoid: Avoid live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu spray) during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last infusion, unless your doctor specifically says it is safe. Avoid being around people who are sick, as your immune system will be weakened. Avoid herpes simplex infections — your doctor will prescribe antiviral medicine to protect you. Women: avoid becoming pregnant during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last infusion, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Avoid grapefruit and alcohol only if your doctor advises it based on other medicines you take. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction (trouble breathing, swelling of face or throat, rapid heartbeat, feeling faint); unusual bruising or bleeding; blood in your urine or very dark urine; signs of infection (fever, chills, severe sore throat, cough); rash, blisters, or peeling skin; yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice); sudden chest pain or shortness of breath; swelling of ankles or legs; signs of thyroid problems (unusual weight changes, feeling very cold or very hot, fast heartbeat); vision changes; headaches that won't go away; confusion or changes in thinking; or any new or unusual symptoms. Regular blood tests and urine tests are REQUIRED every month for 4 years after your last infusion — do NOT skip these appointments, as they detect serious problems early.
when_it_works: Alemtuzumab works differently than daily MS medicines. It does not need to be taken continuously. After your infusions, the medicine works in your body over an extended period of time — often for months to years. Many patients begin to notice improvements or a reduction in MS relapses within months of the first course, but every person responds differently. Your doctor will monitor your progress over time with regular checkups, MRI scans, and lab tests.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant MUST use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while using this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Thyroid disease: This medicine can cause thyroid problems, including a condition called Graves' disease, which can appear years after treatment. Your thyroid will be monitored regularly. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as adjustments to your care may be needed. Elderly patients: Safety and effectiveness in older adults with MS has not been fully established; discuss risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: Lemtrada is not approved for patients under 17 years old. Campath use in children requires specialist guidance.
